Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:11:1.hebrew: דקאמר ניזק ברי לי - ואפ"ה שקיל מן התם, כל שכן דהוה תיובתא דרבה בר נתן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:11:1.english: Where the injured party says, "I am certain" - and even so he takes [payment] from the tam, all the more so that it would be a refutation of Rabba bar Natan.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:12:1.hebrew: אלא דקאמר ניזק שמא - הלכך, מתרווייהו תבע, וכי לא מייתי ראיה, שקיל מן התם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:12:1.english: Rather, where the injured [party] states an uncertain [claim] - Therefore, he claims from both of them, and when he does not bring proof, he collects from the tam [ox].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:13:1.hebrew: רישא נמי ניזק - אומר שמא שורך הזיק, ומזיק אומר ברי בסלע לקה; וכי אפ"ה קאמר סומכוס דחולקין, דאיצטריך לרבנן לאפלוגי ולאשמועינן דלא פלגי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:13:1.english: [In] the first clause also, the injured party - says, "Perhaps your ox caused the damage," and the damager says with certainty, "It was struck by a stone"; and even so, does Sumkhos say that they divide [the payment], such that it was necessary for the Rabbis to disagree and teach us that they do not divide [it]?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:15:1.hebrew: רישא דקאמר מזיק שמא וניזק ברי - והתם אמר סומכוס שהורע כחו של נתבע וחולקין, ואתו רבנן לאשמועינן דלעולם יד נתבע על העליונה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:15:1.english: The first clause, where it states [that] the damager [claims] "perhaps" and the injured party [claims] "certainly" - And there, Sumakhos said that the power of the defendant is weakened and they divide [it], and the Rabbis come to teach us that the defendant always has the upper hand.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:16:1.hebrew: והא לא דמיא רישא לסיפא - וכיון דסוף סוף לאו בחדא מילתא מוקמת להו, שפיר מצי ר' חייא בר אבא לאוקמי לרישא בברי וברי ולמפשט דסומכוס אפי' בברי וברי אמר, ומאי אתקפתיה דרב פפא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:16:1.english: But the first clause is not similar to the last clause - And since ultimately you do not establish them in one [and the same] matter, Rabbi Chiya bar Abba could well establish the first clause as [a case of] "certain" and "certain" [claims] and resolve [that] Sumakhos stated [his ruling] even in [a case of] "certain" and "certain" [claims]; so what was Rav Pappa's objection?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:1:1.english: Both of them are exempt - For both of them push him off [onto the other].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:1:2.english: Both are liable - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:21:1.hebrew: ראוי ליטול - אי מייתי ראיה, ואין לו אי לא מייתי, ולא תדוק מינה כדקדייקת. ולהכי מוקים לה הכי, ולא מוקים לה כדאוקים למציעתא לעיל בניזק שמא ומזיק ברי, דאם כן היינו הך, וסיפא אמאי אצטריך. ורבה, דאוקמא למציעתא דניזק שמא ומזיק ברי, ולא אוקמה בברי וברי ולישני "ראוי ליטול ואין לו", משום דס"ל דסומכוס לא אמר "חולקין" בברי וברי. הלכך, רישא דקתני "לא כי, אלא בסלע לקה" לא אצטריך למיתני' בברי וברי לאשמועינן דמוציא מחבירו כו'; להכי אוקמה למציעתא בשמא וברי, דתיקו נמי רישא בברי ושמא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:21:1.english: It is fitting [for him] to take - If he brings proof; and he has nothing if he does not bring [proof], and do not infer from it as you inferred. And for this reason he establishes it thus, and does not establish it as he established the middle clause earlier, in [a case of] an injured party [claiming] "perhaps" and a damager [claiming] "certainly" — for if so, this is the same [as the middle clause], and why would the latter clause be necessary? And Rabbah, who established the middle clause [as a case] where the injured party [claims] "perhaps" and the damager [claims] "certainly," and did not establish it in [a case of] "certainly" and "certainly" and answer, "It is fitting [for him] to take, and he has nothing" — [did so] because he holds that Sumakhos did not say "they divide" in [a case of] "certainly" and "certainly." Therefore, the first clause, which teaches, "Not so, rather it was injured by a rock," did not need to be taught in [a case of] "certainly" and "certainly" to teach us that [the burden of proof is on] the one who seeks to exact [payment] from his fellow, etc.; for this reason he established the middle clause in [a case of] "perhaps" and "certainly," so that the first clause would also stand in [a case of] "certainly" and "perhaps."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:2:1.english: The large [ox] caused the damage - And its body has the value of half-damages.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:2:2.hebrew: קטן הזיק - ודמי הקטן תקח, ומותר חצי נזק תפסיד:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:2:2.english: The small [ox] caused the damage - And you shall take the value of the small [ox], and you shall lose the remainder of the half-damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:3:1.hebrew: וקטן הזיק את הגדול - ואע"ג שחצי נזקו של גדול מרובה, לא תקח אלא קטן שלי, וחצי נזק של קטן שלך קח מן הגדול:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:3:1.english: And the small [ox] injured the large [ox] - Even though half the damage of the large [ox] is great, you shall take only my small [ox], and half the damage of your small [ox] take from the large [ox].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:4:1.hebrew: על סומכוס - דאמר לקמן (בבא קמא דף מו.) בברייתא בגמ' בשור שנגח את הפרה: ממון המוטל בספק חולקין. וממתני' שמעינן דחלוקים עליו חביריו, דקתני המוציא מחבירו כו':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:4:1.english: With Sumakhos - Who says later (Bava Kamma 46a) in a baraita in the Gemara, in [the chapter] Shor SheNagach Et HaParah: "Property of uncertain ownership is divided." And from our Mishnah we learn that his colleagues disagree with him, as it teaches: "The one who seeks to exact from his fellow," etc.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:5:1.hebrew: אמר סומכוס אפילו ברי וברי - דשניהם טוענים טענת ברי, ואפילו היכא דנתבע טוען "ברי לי שאיני חייב", ואפילו הכי, כיון דלבי דינא מספקא אי קאמר קושטא, חולקין — דקאמרת מתניתין דלא כסומכוס:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:5:1.english: Did Sumakhos state [this] even [in a case of] a certain [claim] and a certain [claim] - That both of them make a claim of certainty, and even where the defendant claims, "I am certain that I am not liable," and even so, since to the court it is doubtful whether he is speaking the truth, they divide — [with reference to] what you said, [that] our Mishnah is not in accordance with Sumakhos.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:6:1.english: Not so - [This] implies that it is certain to him that it was injured by a rock.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:9:1.hebrew: שקיל כדאמר מזיק - וגובה מן התם, ואע"ג דקאמר ניזק ברי לי שזה לא הזיקני:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:9:1.english: He takes according to what the damager says - And he collects from the tam [ox], even though the injured party says, "I am certain that this [ox] did not injure me."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:9:2.hebrew: פטור - אף מדמי שעורין, דהא אמר ליה תובע "לאו שעורין יהבי לך", ואחולי מחיל גביה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35b:9:2.english: Exempt - Even from the value of the barley, for the claimant says to him, "I did not give you barley," and he [thereby] waives [any claim to it] with him.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35b:11:1.hebrew: לימא תיהוי תיובתא דרבה בר נתן - וא"ת: ואמאי לא מוקי לה כר"ג, דאמר בפ' שבועת הדיינין (שבועות דף מ. ושם): "טענו חטין והודה לו בשעורין — פטור, ור"ג מחייב"? וי"ל: דמהדר לאוקמי כרבנן. ועוד י"ל, דרבה בר נתן אמרה למילתיה ככולי עלמא, ולא מחייב ר"ג אלא שבועה; דאי הוה מחייב בדמי שעורים, מנליה לרבה בר נתן דרבנן פליגי עליה בהא? דלמא לענין שבועה דוקא פליגי, דכתיב "כי הוא זה", דבעינן הודאה ממין הטענה! וכי תימא דרבה בר נתן סבר דמהאי טעמא דפטרי רבנן שבועה לא הויא נמי הודאה להתחייב שעורין — הא ליתא, דהא אמרינן בשבועת הדיינין (שם דף מ:): "טענו חטים ושעורים והודה לו באחד מהן — פטור", והתם ודאי לכ"ע חייב במה שטענו, ואפ"ה פטור משבועה! ע"כ נראה דרבה בר נתן לכ"ע פוטר מדמי שעורים, דמשמע ליה דסברא הוא שהוא פטור, כיון שהודה לו שאין חייב לו שעורין ומחל לו; ובשבועה דוקא פליגי אי בעינן ממין הטענה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35b:11:1.english: "Let us say that [it] is a conclusive refutation of Rabba bar Natan" - And if you ask: Why does [the Gemara] not establish [the mishna] in accordance with Rabban Gamliel, who says in the chapter Shevuat HaDayyanin (Shavuot 40a and there [in the Gemara]): "If one claimed wheat from him and he admitted to barley — he is exempt, and Rabban Gamliel obligates [him]"? One can answer that [the Gemara] seeks to establish [it] in accordance with the Rabbis. Furthermore, one can answer that Rabba bar Natan stated his ruling in accordance with everyone, and Rabban Gamliel only obligates [him to take] an oath; for if [Rabban Gamliel] obligated [him] for the value of the barley, from where would Rabba bar Natan know that the Rabbis disagree with him on this? Perhaps they disagree specifically regarding an oath, as it is written, "that this is it" [Exodus 22:8], [indicating] that we require an admission of the same kind as the claim! And if you say that Rabba bar Natan holds that for this [same] reason that the Rabbis exempt [him from] an oath, it is also not [considered] an admission to be obligated [for the] barley — that is not so, for we say in [the chapter] Shevuat HaDayyanin (there, 40b): "If one claimed wheat and barley from him and he admitted to one of them — he is exempt," and there, certainly according to everyone he is obligated [to pay] what he claimed from him, and even so he is exempt from an oath! Therefore, it appears that Rabba bar Natan exempts [him] from the value of the barley according to everyone, for it seems to him that it is logical that he is exempt, since [the claimant] conceded to him that he does not owe him barley and waived it for him; and they disagree specifically regarding an oath, whether we require [an admission] of the same kind as the claim.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35b:13:1.hebrew: מדסיפא ניזק שמא ומזיק ברי רישא נמי כו' ואמר סומכוס כו' - אבל מסיפא גופה ליכא למיפרך, דאיכא למימר: כיון דאיכא הודאה במקצת — שהרי מודה שהקטן הזיקו לכל הפחות — הלכך איכא למימר דקאמר סומכוס חולקים, אע"ג דניזק קאמר שמא ומזיק אמר ברי. ואם תאמר: דנימא "ברי ושמא, ברי עדיף", כדקאמר רב יהודה בהגוזל בתרא (לקמן בבא קמא דף קיח.) גבי "מנה לי בידך" והלה אומר "איני יודע"? ויש לומר: דהתם הוי ברי טוב, שלא יהיה לו פנים לשקר כיון שחבירו יכול לידע בשקרו זה, והשמא אינו טוב, שאין זוכר אם חייב לו, ומוכחא מילתא דחייב לו; אבל הכא ברי שלו גרוע, שיודע בחבירו שאין יכול להכחישו, ולכך טוען ברי, והאי נמי דקאמר שמא — לפי שלא ראה המעשה; הלכך לא אמרינן "ברי עדיף":
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35b:13:1.english: "From [the fact that] the latter clause [is a case of] the injured [party stating] an uncertain [claim] and the damager [stating] a certain [claim], the first clause [is] also, etc., and does Sumakhos say, etc." - However, from the latter clause itself one cannot raise an objection, since one can say [that] because there is a partial admission — for [the damager] admits that the small [ox] damaged it at the very least — therefore one can say that Sumakhos says they divide [the disputed amount], even though the injured [party] states an uncertain [claim] and the damager states a certain [claim]. And if you ask: Let us say [that between] a certain [claim] and an uncertain [claim], the certain [claim] prevails, as Rav Yehuda says in [the chapter] HaGozel Batra (below, Bava Kamma 118a) regarding [one who claims], "I have a maneh in your possession," and the other says, "I do not know"? And one can answer: There it is a strong certain [claim], for he would not have the audacity to lie since his fellow could know of this lie of his, and the uncertain [claim] is not strong, for he does not remember whether he owes him, so it is evident that he owes him; but here his certain [claim] is weak, since he knows of his fellow that he cannot contradict him, and therefore he pleads with certainty, and this one too [who] states an uncertain [claim does so] because he did not witness the incident; therefore we do not say "the certain [claim] prevails."

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35b:15:1.hebrew: רישא במזיק שמא - ואם תאמר: והא "לא כי" קתני? וי"ל דבברי וברי נמי איירי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35b:15:1.english: The first clause [refers to a case] where the one liable for damage [states] an uncertain [claim] - And if you will ask: But [the Mishnah] teaches, "Not so" [which implies a certain denial]! One can answer that it is also dealing with [a case of] a certain [claim] and a certain [claim].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35b:4:1.hebrew: זאת אומרת חלוקים עליו חביריו על סומכוס - דוקא בכי האי גוונא פליג סומכוס, שראוי להסתפק בדבר. וההיא (ב"מ דף ק. ושם) דמחליף פרה בחמור, והמוכר שפחתו וילדה — בכל הנך בלא טענותם ראוי להסתפק לב"ד. אבל במקום שהספק בא ע"פ דבריהם לא פליג סומכוס; דהרי למ"ד אמר סומכוס אפילו ברי וברי, אטו אם אמר אדם לחבירו: "טלית זו שאתה לבוש שלי הוא", מי אמר סומכוס חולקים? ובשנים אוחזים בטלית אמר דאי אתו לקמן כי תפיס חד וחד מיסרך סרוכי, דאפי' לסומכוס סרוכי לאו כלום הוא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35b:4:1.english: That is to say, his colleagues disagree with Sumakhos - Specifically in a case like this does Sumakhos disagree [with the Sages], where it is fitting to be in doubt about the matter. And that [case] (Bava Metzia 100a, and there) of one who exchanges a cow for a donkey, and one who sells his maidservant and she gives birth — in all of these, [even] without their claims, it is fitting for the court to be in doubt. But in a place where the doubt arises based on their words, Sumakhos does not disagree; for behold, [even] according to the one who says [that] Sumakhos said [they divide] even [in a case of] "certain" and "certain" [claims], if a person says to his fellow: "This cloak that you are wearing is mine," did Sumakhos say they divide [it]? And in [the chapter] Shenayim Ochazin BeTalit it says that if they come before us when one is grasping [the cloak] and one is [merely] clinging [to it], even according to Sumakhos, [mere] clinging is nothing.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35b:6:1.hebrew: ממאי דמתני' ברי וברי - וא"ת: והיכא אמרינן דמתני' ברי וברי? אי משום דאמר "אמר סומכוס ברי וברי", היינו משום דאי לא אמר סומכוס בברי וברי, לא היה יכול לדקדק ממשנה דחולקים, דהוי מצי לאוקמי בברי וברי ודברי הכל! וי"ל דה"ק: ממאי דמתני' מצי לאורויי כלל בברי וברי? דלמא בברי ושמא דוקא איירי, כדאמרינן בסמוך דרישא דומיא דסיפא! ומשני: דקתני "זה אומר לא כי". ואף על גב דבפ"ק דכתובות (דף יב: ושם) תנן: "והוא אומר לא כי, אלא עד שלא ארסתיך נאנסת והיה מקחי מקח טעות", ומוכח התם דהיינו שמא — התם ליכא למיטעי, שאין הבעל רגיל לידע; אבל הכא, אי בשמא איירי, לא ה"ל למיתני "לא כי", כיון דאיכא למיטעי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35b:6:1.english: From where [do we know] that the Mishnah [refers to] bari and bari [a certain claim against a certain claim]? - And if you ask: Where did we say that the Mishnah is [a case of] bari and bari? If [you say it is] because he [Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba] said, "Sumkhos said [his ruling even in a case of] bari and bari," that was [only] because if Sumkhos had not said [his ruling] in [a case of] bari and bari, he would not have been able to infer from the Mishnah that [the Sages] disagree [with Sumkhos], for one could have established [the Mishnah] as [referring to] bari and bari, and [thus] according to everyone [even Sumkhos would agree]! And one can answer that this is what [the Gemara] is saying: From where [do we know] that the Mishnah can teach at all [a case of] bari and bari? Perhaps it speaks specifically of bari and shema [a certain claim against an uncertain claim], as we say immediately below that the first clause is similar to the latter clause! [And the Gemara answers:] Because it teaches, "This one says: No, rather..." And even though in the first chapter of Ketubot (12b and there [in the Gemara]) we learned [in a Mishnah]: "And he says: No, rather before I betrothed you, you were violated, and my acquisition was a mistaken acquisition," and it is proven there that this is [a claim of] shema [uncertainty] — there, there is no [concern of] erring, because the husband does not usually know [when it happened]; whereas here, if it were speaking of shema, it should not have taught "No, rather...," since there is [room] to err [and think he is making a certain claim].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35b:9:1.hebrew: הא לא מייתי ראייה שקיל כדאמר מזיק - וא"ת: דלמא הא לא מייתי ראייה לא שקיל מידי? וי"ל: דלשון "המוציא" משמע במה שבא להוציא צריך ראייה, אבל מה שהוא מודה לו — לא. ולקמן דמשני "ראוי ליטול ואין לו", היינו בלא תפס, אבל בתפס יש לו, ולהכי א"ש לשון "המוציא":
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35b:9:1.english: [This implies that] if he does not bring proof, he takes according to what the damager says - And if you say: perhaps if he does not bring proof, he takes nothing? One can answer that the phrasing "the one who seeks to extract" implies [that] regarding that which he comes to extract, he needs proof, but [regarding] that which [the damager] admits to him, he does not. And later, where [the Gemara] answers, "[It means] he is fit to take, and he does not have [it]," that refers to [a case] where he did not seize [it]; but where he seized [it], he has [it], and therefore the phrasing "the one who seeks to extract" fits well.
